{{nihongo|'''Shigariwake Shrine'''|志賀理和気神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

``Shiga Riwake Shrine'' (Shigariwake Jinja/Shikariwake Jinja, Shiga Riwake Shrine) is located in {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|Q48326|qid=Q48326}}{{ill|Shiwa District, Iwate|Q1131886|qid=Q1131886}}{{ill|Shiwa, Iwate|Q387336|qid=Q387336}} Sakuramachi. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=Prefectural company|qid=Q90139226|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.

Also known as ``Akaishi Shrine'' and ``Ukishima Myojin''. It is known for being the northernmost Shikinai shrine.

== Enshrined God ==
The following seven deities are enshrined. </ref>.
* {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286}} (Futunushi no Kami)
* {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchijin}}
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōki no Kami}} (Onamuji no Kami)
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona no Kami}}
* {{ill|Ukemochi|Q2280323|qid=Q2280323}} (Ukemochi no Kami)
* {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahikokami}}
* Funadama no Kami

Among the deities enshrined, five of them, including Okami no Kami, are said to have been enshrined together in later generations.

== History ==

== Founding ==
According to the shrine legend, in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 23rd year ({{ill|804|Q29998|qid=Q29998}}), {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Q941979|qid=Q941979}} was appointed as the guardian deity of Tohoku development. <ref name="historical book"/>.

In the early part of the {{ill|9th century|Q8083|qid=Q8083}}, the area was constructed with {{ill|Shiwa Castle|Q11491083|qid=Q11491083}} ({{ill|803|Q30388|qid=Q30388}}), Shiba District ({{ill|Shiwa District, Iwate|Q1131886|qid=Q1131886}}) construction, {{ill|Tokutan Castle|Q11489487|qid=Q11489487}} construction ({ {jalink|811|Q29946}}) and other areas are being developed, and our company is also working to reward the pacification of {{ill|Emishi|Q932574|qid=Q932574}} and to protect the area. {{Sfn|Shiga Riwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}{{Sfn|Shiga Riwake Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. There are many examples of Shikinai-sha shrines in Ou being built by subsuming the landowner deity and inviting a central deity, but it is not clear whether this is the case for our company, and the origin of the divine name ``Shiga Riwaki'' is also uncertain {{Sfn|Shiga Riwake Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.

== Outline ==
The first appearance in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokukushi}} was in the second year of {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} ({{ill|852|Q30383|qid=Q30383}}), the {{jalink|god of Shigari Wakejin}. The article states that Kana|Q11591025}} was promoted to the lower rank of Shogoi, but judging from the content, it appears to have been a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=government shrine}} that had a divine rank even before Ninju {{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} In "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} alink|Mutsu Province|Q907389}}{{ill|Shiwa District, Iwate|Q1131886|qid=Q1131886|lt=Shiba District}}, it is described as "Shiga Riwake Shrine" and is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}}{{Sfn|Shiga Riwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}. Shigariwake Shrine (Heibonsha) | 1990}} is the only Shikinai shrine in Shiba County and the northernmost Shikinai shrine in Japan.After the collapse of the Ritsuryo system, there are no historical documents from the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, and its condition at that time is not known, but it appears to have fallen into such disrepair that one could even forget that it was a Shikinai shrine.{{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}} Shrine (Gods) | 1984}}, {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} At the beginning of {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it was called ``Akaishi Daimyojin'' because Akaishi was {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} {{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}. A legend about this red stone is that when the lord of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kosui-dera Castle}}, {{ill|Shiba Akinao|Q11500879|qid=Q11500879}}, passed through this area, {{ill|Kitakami River|Q1348297|qid=Q1348297}} There is a red stone at the bottom of the river, and the water waves are purple, so he wrote a poem that goes, ``Rather than Kefu, I would name it Shiwa, because the waves on the stones of this river resemble purple.''{{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}. Because of this, the name of the district was ``Shinami-gun,'' and the name of the shrine was ``Akaishi Daimyojin,'' and it is said that the red stone that was salvaged is still enshrined within the shrine grounds.It is said that in the middle of the {{ill|18th century|Q7015|qid=Q7015}}, the history of the Shikinai shrine was revived and the shrine building was rebuilt.{{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}. {{ill|1785|Q7756|qid=Q7756}} in {{ill|Tenmei|Q1194121|qid=Q1194121}} |Q11619285}}'s travelogue also mentions our company as Shigariwake Shrine, a Shikinai shrine {{Sfn|Shikariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}. In addition, our company was revered by the {{ill|Nanbu clan|Q2975330|qid=Q2975330}}, the lord of the {{ill|Morioka Domain|Q908854|qid=Q908854}}, and was dedicated with the name ``Nanbu Ichi no Miya'' {{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Early modern rituals were once carried out by Akaishiyama Hensho-ji Temple as {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}, and this Hensho-ji Temple had a temple territory of {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 30 koku were given in 7 years ({{ill|1602|Q6727|qid=Q6727}}) {{Sfn|Shigariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}. However, {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Since the temple was abandoned in the Genwa}} years ({{ill|1615|Q6784|qid=Q6784}}-{{ill|1624|Q6821|qid=Q6821}}), the Tamura family of farmers took over for a while, and then Korin-ji Temple became the special charge {{Sfn|Shikariwake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1990}}.After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in October of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} |Q134917316}}, and was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}} on March 26, {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}13 ({{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}}). Furthermore, during this period, the shrine petitioned for promotion to Kokuheisha twice, once in 1908 ({{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}) and again in 2nd year of Taisho ({{ill|1913|Q2080|qid=Q2080}}).

== God level ==
* August 7th, 2nd year of {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} ({{ill|852|Q30383|qid=Q30383}}), the lower rank of the fifth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}'') - Written as ``Shiga Riwakejin.''

== Precincts ==
The approach is lined with about 30 {{ill|Cherry blossom|Q871991|qid=Q871991}} tall trees. The variety is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Azumahigan}}. The largest of these trees is 6 meters and 80 centimeters in circumference at the base, 11 meters and 5 centimeters in height, and is estimated to be about 500 years old. It is believed to be the oldest group of Higanzakura in the prefecture, and has been designated as a natural monument by Shiwa Town as the ``southern cherry tree.''

== Setsusha ==
There are three shrines within the precincts as follows. </ref>.
* Sakashita Inari Shrine
* Onofuji Inari Shrine
* Akaishi Tenmangu Shrine

== Festival ==
* Donto Festival (January 15th)<ref>The description of the festival is based on the shrine history book. </ref>
*Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Prayer Festival (Spring Festival) (April 29th)
* Summer Purification Ceremony (June 30th)
* Doll Festival (June 30th)
* Reitaisai (Autumn Festival) (first Friday, Saturday and Sunday of September)
